name: Search-Led Content Brief
summary: Researches the pages that rank for a keyword, reads the top pages, and writes a content brief that covers their gaps.
description: Searches a keyword or question, reads the top-ranking pages, and summarises what each one covers (quoted), the search intent they serve, the subtopics they share, and what they miss. The brief proposes a title, outline and angle that answer the intent better, with each "competitor covers" point tied to a page that was actually read. Who it's for: content marketers, SEO leads and writers planning an article. Limitations: search results differ by location and personalisation and change over time; it reads pages, not ranking data, so it gives no search volumes or difficulty scores.
problems: I need a content brief for a keyword
I want to know which topics top ranking articles cover

outputs.label: Content brief
outputs.description: Intent, what top pages cover, gaps, title and outline.

execution.system: You are an SEO content strategist. Base what competitors cover on the pages read, quoted; your recommendations are inference built on those gaps. Work only from the retrieved sources and the user's inputs. Every factual statement cites a source id, and quotes are copied exactly. Say what you could not verify.

steps.name: Research
steps.responsibility: Search the web and read the most relevant pages.
steps.prompt: Search this keyword as a searcher would and find the top-ranking articles and guides. Read the leading pages.

steps.name: Write
steps.responsibility: Write the output from the retrieved sources.
steps.prompt: Summarise what each read page covers, citing its id and copying a supporting passage exactly into quote. Identify gaps none of them cover well, then propose a title and outline that serves the intent better. Keep the title under 65 characters.

steps.name: Check sources
steps.responsibility: Citations point to retrieved sources and quotes match them.

tools.purpose: Finds current public sources for the task.
Reads the most relevant results in full so claims rest on page text, not snippets.

criteria.description: Competitor coverage quotes pages read in full.
At least two different pages were analysed.
